speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: How the common areas in the public housing estates are managed, therefore, is a point of tremendous public interest.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In the beginning, HDB and its predecessor, SIT, not only built flats but also managed the common property within the housing estates.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There are various reasons for this, I will mention three of them.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: First, it holds the elected Members of Parliament to account for, and also gives their residents a greater say in, the management of the common property within the public housing estates, that is, local political accountability.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Second, it allows for each town to develop its own distinctive character and instil in the residents an enhanced sense of belonging and pride in their immediate surroundings, that is, community and identity.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Third, by replacing a top-down central management approach with a divested organisation structure, it will allow for a faster turnaround to address residents' complaints, that is, efficiency through decentralisation.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Over the years, Town Council operations have evolved.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Apart from the routine repairs, servicing and maintenance and so on, Town Councils also undertake improvement and upgrading works funded, either fully or substantially, by the Government.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Town Councils derive their revenue from two sources.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: First, service and conservancy charges (S&CC) collected from residents and tenants of commercial units within the township.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This forms the bulk of the funding for estate management.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: This is allocated based on the number of HDB flat units and flat types.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: We also have Good and Services Tax (GST) subvention grants.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There are also separate grants which may only be used in relation to lifts.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: They are the Lift Enhancement Programme, Matching Grant for Lift Replacement Fund and Lift Maintenance Grant.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The question is whether it can work even better today and whether it will remain high functioning tomorrow, especially in light of certain developments which I will now proceed to highlight.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: First, HDB Build-To-Order (BTO) flats in mature estates.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Since 2001, HDB has undertaken many BTO development projects to address the housing needs of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: One driver for this is that it allows young couples starting families an opportunity to purchase BTO units near their parents, who may be living in the older part of the township.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Upon completion, the Town Council will have to manage the new BTO developments in addition to the mature estate.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: In accordance with HDB's mission "to deliver affordable homes of quality and value", our BTO developments give private condominium developers a run for their money.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There are so many beautiful features packed into our BTO developments.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I have reviewed several brochures issued by HDB for BTO developments in mature estates highlighting these features.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Be sheltered from the hustle and bustle of urban life with the central green spine that runs through the development, connecting the surrounding park connectors to form a green network.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Residents can stroll along the green spine or relax in the resting shelters along the way." No doubt, these enhancements were, and are still, being driven by rising expectations of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: An issue arises when we realise that maintenance costs for these extra features in the BTO developments are also "enhanced".

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: These features are not found in mature HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I recently filed a Parliamentary Question with MND asking about maintenance costs for these BTO estates and what steps are taken to ensure that they are within the average maintenance costs undertaken by Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The hon Minister made several points, of which I will highlight two in my speech.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: First, he said that Town Councils are consulted prior to tender.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Respectfully, based on my personal checks, it seems HDB did not undertake this as de rigour.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I am personally aware of instances where such consultation did not happen.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The hon Minister also said that HDB's estimates may differ from Town Councils' estimates as Town Councils may enjoy economies of scale.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Respectfully, where there are BTO flats in mature estates, the situation is usually the opposite.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: All the "verdant green gardens", "green spines" and so on described in the brochures would have to be maintained, not by general landscaping contractors, which is the usual case in mature HDB estates, but specialist contractors.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: For high-rise BTO skyscrapers, HDB has installed pressure reducing valves at various floors of each block.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Town Councils are to regularly check the valves and run diagnostics when residents encounter problems, such as "water hammering".

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: There is no such issue arising in mature estates.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: On a final example, Sir, may I have your permission to show an object?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: These pavers were used to pave the driveways in a BTO housing estate.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: To replace them and ensure the same look and feel, the Town Council would have to purchase them from the UK.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: With respect to the hon Minister, there is no economy of scale that Town Councils can leverage for these costs.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I am not making an argument to trade off aesthetics for costs.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: All I am asking for is a deeper reflection on the implication of each decision at the construction and design stage.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This cannot happen unless our policy sets the right regulatory incentives.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Our current model may have some tension, as I shall explain.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Prior to 1989, since HDB would have been in charge of both developing and maintaining the housing estate, it would be able to get a better sense of the maintenance costs for developments and factor that in, directly, because, ultimately, HDB has to balance its books.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Thirty years later, it seems to me that there are warning signs that this ability may have hollowed out or that it is not foremost in the minds of the officers, given that there is no incentive to look at maintenance, only development.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: What I have described has the hallmarks of, or, if not an outright moral hazard, at least a misalignment of incentives developing between HDB and the Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: While not contradictory, we can appreciate that what motivates a developer is not what motivates a maintenance contractor.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: One thing that needs to be appreciated is that townships managed by Town Councils are not homogenous.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Where a Town Council entirely manages a non-mature BTO estate, there may be no issue.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: But, where a single Town Council manages an estate comprising both mature HDB estates and BTO developments, the situation can be markedly different and, therefore, must be addressed.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The question of parity and fairness needs to be asked.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I had earlier explained the structure of S&CC grants from the Government.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: It does not take into account the higher maintenance costs of BTO flats with these unique features that are not found in mature estates.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: On the other hand, S&CC by residents are all put in a common pool and fixed, based on flat type.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: There is no uplift in S&CC for BTO units in the by-laws passed by all 17 Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Owners of DBSS units are charged higher S&CC, but that is not directly relevant here.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This raises an issue of equity which must be addressed immediately.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: As it stands, costs for maintaining Town Council estates have been escalating whilst revenue is, generally, flat.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: If this carries on, Town Councils will be looking to raise S&CC.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The equity issue must be dealt with first.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The potential issue of cross-subsidisation also rears its head when dealing with problems associated with BTO design features in common properties.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I recently filed a Parliamentary Question highlighting the problem of slippery and wet drop-off points, walkways and so on at HDB BTO developments arising from design issues.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The hon Minister suggested that such feedback can be channelled by the Town Council to HDB and HDB will decide how best to deal with these matters.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The response by HDB was that the Town Council should undertake the recommended works using Community Improvement Projects Committee (CIPC).

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This exacerbates the cross-funding issue that I highlighted earlier.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: All things being equal, CIPC should be utilised to build facilities at the mature estates.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Many of them were originally built without drop-off points and sheltered walkways and did not address design limitations of built features at these new BTO units.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I now turn to the Town Council's responsibility in maintaining infrastructures at common properties in mature estates.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: There is a lifecycle involved beyond which they must be renewed.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: For each infrastructure, there is also a built-in tolerance limit beyond which the infrastructure may have to be strengthened or repaired.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: For works to upgrade infrastructure to last beyond its lifecycle or repairs to infrastructure damaged because tolerance limits are exceeded, it is my respectful view that Town Councils should not be undertaking such projects if they are to be funded by S&CC.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Residents' S&CC should be used for maintenance per se and not be used to replace or extend the life of such infrastructural works.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This should be the case even if the Government funds 90% of the costs through CIPC, leaving 10% to be funded by S&CC.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Again, recently, I filed a Parliamentary Question to understand the Ministry's position on whose responsibility it is to repair scupper drains around mature estates, which have been misaligned owing to soil movements.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: The hon Minister's position is that the responsibility lies with the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I accept that one possible solution is incorporating these works through the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) which is 100% funded by the Government.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: But this is not an elegant solution, because NRP cycles do not coincide with infrastructure life cycles or timed to occur when repairs are needed because infrastructure tolerances are exceeded.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Also, the NRP budget is finite and residents may not necessarily be happy that the budget is utilised to repair drains or other parts of the infrastructure when it can be used to renew amenities, such as playgrounds, BBQ pits and so on.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I pause here to summarise the three main points I have made so far, so that hon Members can see the solution that may already be emanating.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: First, having Town Councils separate from HDB creates two sets of incentives – one for the developer and one for the maintenance contractor.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: These incentives can be perverse in some cases.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: From a purely economic point of view, Town Councils can achieve less economies of scale.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Second, the issue of parity between old flats and new ones becomes important, and the drawing of lines becomes less that of a town, than that of old estates versus new.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In this case, the boundaries of a town become less relevant than the type of flats.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Third and related to the boundaries issue, the same argument arises for the blurring of boundaries between maintaining old infrastructure and building new ones.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Given this, a question that begs to be asked is this: is the "town" the right boundary, or the right unit of measurement, for such works?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Aside from the three points above which relate to mainly infrastructure, I now come to the issue of human resource management at Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Anecdotally, I have noted that there is a relatively high turnover amongst all Town Councils at the level of resident-facing property officers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: These officers form the backbone of all Town Councils.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: They are the ones who, on a day-to-day basis, ensure that rubbish is duly collected every day from each block, common areas are swept and cleaned, the lifts are working and the various issues that pop up without notice from time to time are attended to.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Having spoken to several of them and their managers, the common grouses are tough work conditions and the lack of career prospects from within the organisation.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: For property officers employed directly by Town Councils, the sense amongst them is that the organisations are too small to accommodate their personal growth.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: For the property officers who are employed by the management agents of Town Councils, the scale issue may be addressed by the management agents' ability to deploy property officers across properties that they maintain.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Still, however, the management agents lose property officers to bigger organisations, such as HDB, which values their skills and experience.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: In the pre-1989 situation, HDB would have been the employer of these property officers.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Doubtless, it is a much bigger organisation which would have allowed for these officers to attend skills upgrading, provide regular career progression and even lateral transfers to other areas of operations.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: If we are serious about wanting to ensure a reasonable standard of maintenance in our public housing estates, the human resource management issue must be tackled decisively.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: There must be an Industry Transformation Map for this sector.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: We need to build a deeper pool of expertise in management of townships.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I am not suggesting that this is a broken system now.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: But if we do not do anything, I fear it will be.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: So, what areas should the hon Minister be looking at?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: We recall that the three main motivations for the Town Council are – local political accountability, community and identity, and efficiency through decentralisation.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This will reduce opportunities for the misalignment of incentives I spoke about.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: It will eliminate turf wars that happen from time to time between HDB and Town Councils on issues, such as source of water leaks, whether from external walls or from within the units.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: It will also allow for the provision of maintenance services at a much higher economy of scale and a deeper level of expertise.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: This will, in turn, taper the increase in maintenance costs.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: We also will have an opportunity to convince property officers to stay in their jobs, because their employer is a big organisation that will invest heavily in the upgrading of their skills, and provide promotion and transfer opportunities.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Issues of turnaround time for a centralised body to deal with complaints, which was a problem in the 1980s, can be managed more effectively now through advances in technology.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Of course, we also have the Municipal Services Office.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: Such works will enable the Town Council to develop its precinct's own unique character.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai
text: I look forward to hearing the hon Minister's response to my speech.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Let us revisit the rationale for forming Town Councils, which we did back in 1989.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The purpose was to give elected Members of Parliament the autonomy to run their own towns and, thereby, let towns develop a distinctive character, guided by the needs of residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is also a testing ground for Members of Parliament to win, and retain, the trust and confidence of their residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Not only are Members of Parliament expected to represent voters in Parliament, they are also required to pay close attention to the management and maintenance of our HDB estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: This is a role that comes with custodial and financial responsibilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is a uniquely Singapore approach to governance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The simplest way to describe the relationship between HDB and Town Councils is that the former builds while the latter does everything else – manages, maintains, replaces and repairs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: To fund these activities, the Town Council collects Service and Conservancy Charges (S&CC) from HDB households.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, the Government does not leave it to Town Councils to raise the funds required from HDB households alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Second, the Government provides additional funding for replacing or maintaining major infrastructural items, such as the Lift Replacement Matching Grant and the Lift Enhancement Programme (LEP).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Third, major efforts to renew HDB towns are heavily funded or even undertaken by the Government through dedicated programmes like the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme (NRP) or Remaking Our Heartlands (ROH).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It is understandable for Town Councils to question whether the parameters under which they operate are fair and reasonable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They are subject to laws and regulations and are also accountable to residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I see the hon Member's speech in this light and welcome it.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The key points raised by the Member are tension between HDB's role in building and Town Councils' role in maintaining public housing estates, and whether HDB or the Government can undertake the maintenance of public housing estates.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I will address these and the other points made by the Member about Town Councils' challenges and financial sustainability.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: First, the Member expressed concerns about the maintenance costs of features in new BTO developments, some of which have higher maintenance costs, due to the need for specialist contractors or equipment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Sustainability and maintainability are factors that HDB considers when designing new BTO projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: BTO projects adopt design for maintainability principles, including the appropriate choice of materials and finishes and proper detailing for durability and maintenance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB also seeks Town Councils' feedback on whether there are features that may affect maintenance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: That said, many other factors besides downstream maintenance costs, are considered at the design stage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Otherwise, we would end up with cookie-cutter precincts that cannot reflect the aspirations of homeowners or the changing demands of urban living.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The building of skyrise greenery is a good example.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Incorporating more greenery into our compact and high-rise urban environment is an important solution for tackling urban heat.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But such features must be thoughtfully designed to keep maintenance costs manageable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The key is to ensure good feedback loops between HDB and Town Councils pre-tender and during construction, so that adjustments can be made promptly to address potential maintenance issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Such feedback loops should continue after residents move in and add to HDB's experience when designing subsequent projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We value the Member's feedback and will review our processes to ensure that ease of maintenance is given due priority.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We also agree that HDB should deal with design issues that might not have been evident upstream and which present themselves upon project completion promptly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Regarding the dislodged pavers that the Member has mentioned, indeed, there were issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: HDB has incorporated this learning and will avoid using such pavers in future projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Member has suggested that the Government should fund the costs of replacing infrastructure beyond its lifecycle, and repairs to infrastructure damaged because tolerance limits are exceeded.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Today, Town Councils can already fund such cyclical works through the Sinking Fund and, for lifts, through the Lift Replacement Fund.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Hence, the Government already co-funds such infrastructural works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The use of S&CC to defray cyclical maintenance and replacement costs in HDB estates is no different from the practice in private condominiums where maintenance fees are used to pay for the cyclical maintenance and replacement of infrastructure, except that the Government provides significant support for public housing – both in terms of funding and otherwise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Town Councils should, thus, continue to set aside funds from S&CC collected for long-term cyclical replacement works.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We further provide S&CC rebates directly to residents, to help those who require more assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We recognise that Town Councils face various cost pressures, due to a mix of internal and external factors, including tightening manpower, economic uncertainties caused by the pandemic and global supply chain disruptions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Ultimately, any long-term increases in costs will have to be borne in one way or another by all of us.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Nonetheless, let me assure the Member that the Government will continue to partner Town Councils closely in this endeavour.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Member has highlighted the high turnover of Town Council property officers due to tough working conditions and lack of career prospects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Manpower challenges are not unique to Town Councils and are faced by organisations across Singapore, including the public sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: We recognise the demanding nature of property officers' work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: They need to have the technical competency to maintain infrastructure and also soft skills to manage multiple stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: The Government has, thus, been providing significant support to help Town Council officers acquire the necessary skills to handle their work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These include: (a) regular training and sharing sessions to deepen their technical and case management skills; (b) providing technical advice for complex maintenance cases; and (c) establishing clear progression pathways for the facilities management (FM) workforce, including Town Council property officers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Under the Built Environment Skills Framework, FM workers can improve competencies in key transformation areas through training and advance to higher wage bands.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: As some maintenance issues like cleanliness are attributable to human factors, we also strive to tackle these upstream and promote positive behavioural norms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: For example, the Municipal Services Office has been coordinating public education efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: These include strengthening norms that discourage high-rise littering and pigeon feeding.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: It represents an important partnership between the elected Members of Parliament and the residents in co-creating their living environment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: An effective Town Council can build a town into a distinctive, cohesive and vibrant community with a unique identity that is endearing to its residents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: I am heartened that the Member seeks to improve upon our unique approach to local governance and set out his views in a detailed and thoughtful speech.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: However, we would think very carefully before re-centralising township maintenance, as the Member has suggested because devolution is at the heart of the Town Council concept.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: But the Member has provided very helpful reminders to HDB and MND on giving due priority to maintenance costs when designing and building HDB towns and keeping a close track on how the costs of running HDB estates should be managed and apportioned between different stakeholders.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for National Development (Ms Sim Ann)
text: Township management is perhaps not the most exciting of topics, but one that affects the day-to-day experience of many Singaporeans.
